title: Virginia's 2nd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Virginia's 2nd Congressional District, anchored in Hampton Roads and encompassing Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, Suffolk, Franklin, and the Eastern Shore, is one of the most competitive House seats in the nation. Incumbent Republican Jen Kiggans, a former Navy helicopter pilot and nurse practitioner first elected in 2022, is seeking a third term in a district that has flipped between parties repeatedly in recent cycles. Democrats view this as a top pickup opportunity, with a four-candidate primary field including former Rep. Elaine Luria seeking a rematch. The district's large military, veteran, and federal employee population makes it particularly sensitive to national issues such as government shutdowns, defense spending, and health care policy.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 general election in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District. Cook Political Report rates the race as a 'Tossup' as of May 8, 2026.

candidates.name: Jennifer Kiggans
candidates.summary: Jen Kiggans is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Virginia's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2022. She served 10 years as a U.S. Navy helicopter pilot and later became a board-certified Adult-Geriatric Primary Care Nurse Practitioner. Before Congress, she served in the Virginia State Senate from 2020 to 2022, and sits on the House Armed Services, Veterans' Affairs, and Natural Resources Committees.

candidates.name: Elaine Luria
candidates.summary: Elaine Luria is a former U.S. Representative for Virginia's 2nd Congressional District (2019-2023) and a Democratic candidate for the seat in 2026. A retired Navy commander who served for 20 years, she was one of the first female sailors to serve her entire career on combat ships and commanded Assault Craft Unit TWO. She served on the House Select Committee investigating the January 6 Capitol attack and has focused her campaign on lowering costs, improving health care, and national security.

candidates.name: Nila Devanath
candidates.summary: Dr. Nila Devanath is a hospital physician and former attorney running for the Democratic nomination in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District. She grew up in Hampton Roads as the daughter of immigrants and previously practiced law defending survivors of domestic violence at a legal-aid clinic. As an acute-care physician serving veterans and active-duty military families, her campaign emphasizes universal healthcare, reproductive freedom, and lowering costs for working families.

candidates.name: Patrick Mosolf
candidates.summary: Patrick Mosolf is a former USAID official and first-time congressional candidate running in the Democratic primary for Virginia's 2nd Congressional District. He has worked internationally on democracy promotion, election monitoring, humanitarian interventions, and governance in countries including Cambodia, Liberia, Lebanon, Bangladesh, and Burma. His campaign focuses on restoring democratic institutions, addressing cost-of-living issues, and bringing extensive governance and anti-corruption experience to Congress.

candidates.name: Bill Fleming
candidates.summary: Bill Fleming is a Democratic candidate running for Virginia's 2nd Congressional District. He serves as Conservation Director for the Virginia Dare Soil and Water Conservation District representing Virginia Beach, to which he was elected in 2019. Fleming previously ran as a Democratic candidate for Virginia Attorney General in 2021.

candidates.name: Makiba Gaines
candidates.summary: Makiba Gaines is an independent candidate for U.S. House in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District. She is a practicing civil rights attorney based in Norfolk, Virginia, with experience in federal and state criminal appeals. Gaines describes herself as a Christian, wife, and mother, and has also declared candidacy for Virginia's 3rd Congressional District.

candidates.name: Bishop Staten
candidates.summary: Bishop Staten is an independent candidate for U.S. House in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District. Based in the Hampton Roads region, he has also run for Suffolk Commissioner of Revenue. He registered his principal campaign committee with the FEC in December 2025.

candidates.name: DeVinche Albritton
candidates.summary: DeVinche Albritton is an independent candidate for U.S. House in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District who is currently incarcerated. He was convicted of abduction and rape in Virginia Beach and claims innocence, running his campaign from prison with a focus on criminal justice reform. His candidacy is considered highly unusual for a federal office.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling exists for this race, and the Democratic primary (featuring four candidates including former Rep. Elaine Luria) remains unsettled as of June 20, 2026 — both factors compelling low confidence. The district is described as 'one of the most competitive House seats in the nation' and has flipped between parties repeatedly. Cook Political Report rates it 'Tossup' (May 2026). Incumbent Jen Kiggans holds a narrow edge from incumbency and prior success (defeated Luria in 2022 and won re-election in 2024), but Luria — a former two-term representative who previously held the seat — is a strong potential general-election challenger. With zero polling, a competitive primary still unfolding, and a closely divided district sensitive to national headwinds (military/veteran/federal workforce), neither party has a clear advantage, making Tossup the appropriate rating with only a slight Republican lean for incumbency.
